issues.claim: It starts the application's real entry point on an in-memory `TestServer`: requests from the `HttpClient` returned by `CreateClient()` go through the whole middleware pipeline without opening a network port, and services can be replaced with `ConfigureTestServices`.
issues.problem: The correct option is noticeably longer and more detailed than the distractors, which is a test-wiseness tell. The facts are correct. TestServer is the default host. .NET 10 adds only an opt-in UseKestrel, so 'by default' in option b stays accurate. ConfigureTestServices does run after the app's registrations. The fetched excerpt is truncated before the ConfigureTestServices and WithWebHostBuilder text, but I confirm these claims from my own knowledge of the page.
issues.suggestedFix: Shorten option a, for example: 'Starts the app's real entry point on an in-memory `TestServer`: `CreateClient()` requests pass through the full pipeline without a network port.' Keep ConfigureTestServices in the answer and explanation.

issues.claim: schema constraints such as foreign keys and unique indexes are not checked; ... by default starting one throws because of the `TransactionIgnoredWarning` warning
issues.problem: The visible excerpts show support for no transactions, no raw SQL, fewer supported queries, and the 'same issues as SQLite' (including case sensitivity). They do not show the FK/unique-index claim or the TransactionIgnoredWarning behaviour. Both claims are correct (the in-memory provider does not enforce FKs or unique indexes, and BeginTransaction throws by default via InMemoryEventId.TransactionIgnoredWarning), but they are not backed by the cited pages. Both link fetches also returned 429 in the mechanical check, though the excerpts later report status ok.
issues.suggestedFix: Add the 'Testing without your production database system' page (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/ef/core/testing/testing-without-the-database) as a third link with a linkTitle in both locales. That page covers in-memory limitations.
